first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, I prioritize the intervention that addresses two of the three concurrent problems (falling activation and falling onboarding completion) simultaneously, rather than reacting to competitor pricing pressure with a promotional-pricing response that risks margin erosion and a race-to-bottom dynamic with unclear long-term qualified-revenue impact. memory_31 and memory_86 both point to onboarding/activation improvements from self-serve SMB flows and are the most directly relevant, low-cost-to-verify memories given the current metric declines, so I want to confirm their original experiment conditions (segment, definition of 'durable lift', any tradeoffs on lead quality) still match today's context before committing capacity. Promotional pricing (memory_73) and referral incentives (memory_57) remain plausible future levers but are not chosen this week: pricing responses carry higher downstream revenue-quality risk and referral incentives don't address the acute activation/onboarding drops. I'm running this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout because current metrics may reflect a different environment (competitive pressure, changed traffic mix) than when memory_31/memory_86 were consolidated, so replication should be confirmed before scaling.

final.rationale: Both source records confirm the direction: exp_31 shows signup simplification lifts SMB activation (+9%) and net qualified revenue (+4%) despite a small retention dip (-1%), explicitly not replicated outside SMB; exp_86 shows shortened onboarding improves completion (+13%), time-to-value, and retention (+3%) with no noted downside. Combined, these directly target both of this quarter's declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) and are supported by clean, confirmed experimental evidence rather than inference. I'm flagging downstream_value_risk because exp_31's -1% retention tradeoff means the SMB signup-simplification lever, while net positive on qualified revenue historically, has a real (if small) retention cost that should be monitored this cycle, especially since a competitor is aggressively targeting price-sensitive SMB accounts right now — any retention softness compounds competitive churn risk. I'm choosing standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, and current market conditions (competitor pricing pressure) differ from the original test environment, so results should be re-validated at moderate scale before wider commitment. I'm deferring promotional_pricing (memory_73) despite competitive pressure because a reactive pricing war risks eroding qualified revenue quality long-term and wasn't verified this round; it remains a candidate for a future slot if onboarding/activation fixes don't offset competitive SMB losses.
